title: Infosys Cuts FY27 Growth Outlook Despite Strong AI Revenue Surge
excerpt: Infosys trimmed FY27 constant-currency growth guidance to 1-2% after Q2 revenue beat estimates, even as large deal wins hit $5.2 billion and AI revenue jumped 29% quarter on quarter.
body:
• Infosys cut its FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1-2%, down from 1.5-3%, while holding its operating margin outlook at 20-22%.
  • Second-quarter revenue rose 10.7% year on year to Rs 49,244 crore ($5.19 billion), marginally ahead of the Rs 49,132 crore LSEG consensus, but net profit of Rs 7,823 crore missed the Rs 7,929 crore estimate.
  • Large deal wins reached $5.2 billion in the quarter, including a mega deal above $2 billion, and AI revenue grew 29% quarter on quarter to 10.5% of total revenue.
  • Shareholders get an interim dividend of Rs 26 per share, up from Rs 23 a year earlier, with a record date of 3 November 2026 and payment on 11 November 2026.

Infosys lowered its full-year revenue growth forecast on Friday, even as the Bengaluru-based company beat quarterly revenue estimates, signed $5.2 billion in large deals and reported a sharp rise in artificial intelligence revenue. The revision sets up a familiar tension for India's second-largest IT services firm: a strong order book and fast-growing AI work, set against slow conversion into reported growth.

The company now expects revenue for the fiscal year ending March 2027 to grow 1-2% in constant currency, down from 1.5-3% previously, according to its results reported by The Hindu BusinessLine. Operating margin guidance was retained at 20-22%.

Quarterly numbers

Revenue for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 rose 10.7% year on year to Rs 49,244 crore, or $5.19 billion. In constant currency, which strips out exchange-rate movements, growth was 1.5% year on year and 1.2% sequentially. Energy and utilities led the improvement, with revenue from that vertical rising 7.3% year on year in constant-currency terms.

Net profit rose 6.2% year on year to Rs 7,823 crore, below the Rs 7,929 crore analysts had expected on LSEG-compiled estimates. Operating margin held steady at 21%, matching the year-ago level. Basic earnings per share rose 8.7% to Rs 19.32. Free cash flow was $928 million, which chief financial officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said represented 113.3% of net profit.

"We had strong large deals of $5.2 billion, including a mega deal of over $2 billion, reinforcing our position as a trusted partner in the marketplace when clients embark on large and complex transformation programs."

— Salil Parekh, CEO and Managing Director, Infosys

AI growth, slower translation

AI accounted for 10.5% of revenue in the quarter and grew 29% from the previous quarter, the company said. Large deal total contract value of $5.2 billion compared with $3.1 billion in the year-ago quarter, and 62% of the new tally was net new business. The quarter also included client work cited by the company across supply chain, enterprise transformation and IT modernisation, including engagements with Mondelez International and a 10-year agreement with Crocs.

The guidance cut points to the gap between signing work and billing it. Across India's $315 billion IT industry, clients are tying more fees to technology-led productivity gains rather than hours worked, a shift that can lift deal announcements while pressing on traditional revenue lines. Peers Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech also met revenue estimates earlier in the week, with investors rewarding their AI revenue growth.

Segments and geographies

Financial services remained the largest vertical at 28% of quarterly revenue, followed by manufacturing at 16% and energy, utilities, resources and services at 14.2%. Life sciences grew fastest in reported terms, up 32.5% year on year, while hi-tech contracted 17.5% and retail fell 8.1%. North America accounted for 54.6% of revenue, Europe 32.5% and India 2.8%.

Headcount stood at 332,542 on 30 September, up from 328,062 at the end of June. Voluntary attrition eased to 12.7% on a trailing 12-month basis, from 13% in the previous quarter and 14.3% a year earlier. The active client base rose to 2,060.

What investors watch next

Infosys shares closed flat in Mumbai ahead of the results, while a basket of IT stocks fell 0.3%. The test for the second half is conversion: whether the $5.2 billion deal haul, and the mega deal above $2 billion within it, begins to lift constant-currency growth back toward the top of the new 1-2% range. For dividend holders, the Rs 26 interim dividend has a record date of 3 November 2026 and will be paid on 11 November 2026.
